  "text": "On Saturday Mara sold the last of the dining chairs to a woman who wanted to know whether they had belonged to anyone.

‘Presumably,’ Mara said, then wished she had answered differently.

The woman sat on each chair in turn. She chose the one nearest the door and asked Mara to keep the others until her husband could bring the car. After she left, Mara found a glove on the chosen chair. It was too small to be the woman’s, though she had not noticed it before.

She put it in the drawer with the keys that fitted nothing in the shop.

At four her brother rang. She let the phone finish while she helped the woman’s husband carry the chairs outside. He had brought a car that could accommodate two of them. They stood on the pavement considering this.

‘She said they were little,’ he said.

Mara took two chairs back inside.

When she returned the call, her brother asked whether she still accepted donations.

‘It isn’t a charity shop.’

‘I know that.’

‘It depends what they are.’

He said he was making some room. Behind him she could hear a cupboard closing, then opening again.

She asked if he had eaten. He said there was bread.

After they hung up, Mara turned the two remaining chairs towards each other. The shop looked less empty that way, although there was now nowhere sensible to put the fern. She moved it onto the counter and felt the soil with one finger.

Outside, the woman’s husband drove past without stopping. He raised a hand, perhaps to indicate that he would be back."
